*Window: 14 days. 1 post-platform row with data. Generated by `Analytics/report.py`
via the `media-report` skill. **Sample size: one post.** Everything below is direction,
not verdict.*

## 1. Headline

**A stranger liked the post.** That is the first verified organic engagement this
project has ever recorded, and on the metric ladder it matters more than any view
count here. Beyond that: the first post of the new system is doing **5.6× the account's lifetime per-post reach**
(222 views against a 39-views-per-post average across the prior 17 posts), which means
TikTok is not suppressing this account the way the baseline collapse suggested. But it
has produced **zero comments on a post explicitly built to earn comments**, so the
premise this batch was built on is not landing yet. The one genuinely alarming number is
YouTube: **three consecutive days of zero views** while videos were publishing.

## 2. What is working

**Distribution on TikTok.** The single data point:

| Post | Series | Hook | CTA | Views | Likes | Comments | Shares |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| "You didn't quit tracking because you're lazy" | S3 | RIGHTWRONG | COMMENT | 222 | 1 | 0 | 0 |

Published 08:03, measured at T+4h. Trajectory: 183 views at T+3h, 222 at T+4h, then flat
over the last five minutes, so it is already decaying.

That 222 is the only real positive in this report, and it is worth being precise about
what it does and does not show. It shows **the account can still get distribution** —
after the July 22 collapse that was an open question, and it mattered more than any
content question. It does **not** show that S3, the RIGHTWRONG hook, the STORY-BEAT
recipe or the 08:00 slot are good. One post cannot separate those five variables. Every
"BY ..." cut in the script output is the same single row wearing different labels.

## 3. What is not working

**Engagement, and this is the important section.**

- 222 views produced **0 comments**, on a post carrying a COMMENT CTA ("Which day do you
  usually stop?") and a pinned prompt ("day 4 for me, every single time. what day gets
  you?"). Both mechanisms fired and neither converted.
- 1 like, **CONFIRMED ORGANIC** (Connor verified it is not his). This is the **first
  verified response from a stranger in the project's history**. Every previous like,
  comment and follow on every platform traced back to us. On the metric ladder this
  single like outranks all 895 TikTok views, because it is the first evidence that the
  content can move somebody who does not know us.
- 0 shares, 0 saves, 0 new followers.

This is **weak content, not weak distribution**. 222 people saw it; the ceiling on
response was never the problem. The batch hypothesis was that behaviour and psychology
content would earn the comments trivia never did. Four hours in, on one post, it has not.
Not disproven, but not supported either, and TikTok engagement usually arrives with views
rather than trailing them.

**YouTube is the anomaly worth separating from content entirely.** 424 lifetime views,
5 subscribers, and daily views of **0 on July 23, 24 and 25** despite three videos
publishing in that window. Videos going out and registering nothing for three straight
days is not a content-quality pattern. Treat every YouTube reach number as suspect until
this resolves.

**Instagram has no data yet.** 50 lifetime impressions, 1 follower, and the 4 comments in
the account total are **ours, not viewers'** (confirmed by Connor this morning; the
earlier reading that treated Instagram as the more engaged audience is retracted). Our
first Instagram post publishes at 12:30, 25 minutes after this report.

**Facebook returns nulls** — still not linked in Upload-Post.

**One data caveat:** the daily timeseries shows 07-25 = 29 views while the post itself
reports 222. The account-level series lags the per-post API. Trust the per-post number.

## 4. What I would change

**Nothing about the content yet, and that is the recommendation.** One post at T+4h
cannot justify changing a series, hook family, recipe or slot, and `SERIES.md` requires
two weeks and four posts before any scale/iterate/kill verdict. Changing course now would
be exactly the overfitting the loop was built to prevent.

Four things that *are* actionable:

1. **Investigate YouTube separately.** Three days of zero views is a channel-level
   question, not a creative one. Worth checking the channel's standing directly in
   YouTube Studio rather than through the Upload-Post aggregate. Today's 17:00 Short is
   the clean test: if it also reads zero tomorrow, the problem is the channel.
2. **Confirm whether that 1 like is ours.** It is the difference between 0.45% engagement
   and literally zero, and between "someone responded" and "nobody has ever responded."
3. **Let the weekend run untouched.** Six more publishes are queued across three
   platforms, including the first Instagram data this project has ever produced. By
   Sunday evening there will be roughly 9 rows instead of 1, which is the point at which
   the cuts start meaning something.
4. **Hold the comment-earning bias for one more batch.** If Sunday's report still shows
   zero comments across ~9 posts, that is enough evidence to change the approach: the
   next move would be asking a far smaller, dumber question (a one-word answer, an A-or-B)
   rather than an open-ended reflective one.

**Sprint checkpoint:** W31 target is 100 DMs, 3+ creator deals, 1+ creator post live, and
"any comments at all." On the last of those we are at zero. The creator engine has not
started, so the daily DM batch firing is the higher-leverage thread right now.
